sources.title: Five Questions to Ask Before You Invest
sources.text:
Research shows that con-artists are experts at the art of persuasion, often using a variety of influence tactics tailored to the vulnerabilities of their victims. Smart investors check the background of anyone promoting an investment opportunity, even before learning about the opportunity itself.

Investor.gov has a free and simple search tool that allows you to find out if an investment professional is licensed and registered, and if they have a disciplinary history or customer complaints. It’s a great first step toward protecting your money.

sources.title: Budgeting basics: The 50-30-20 rule
sources.text:
Options to save for the future at UNFCU include savings accounts and share certificates.

The 50-30-20 rule is just one way to consider organizing your budget. To find the perfect fit for your situation, consult a professional financial planner.

You subscribe to a streaming service to watch your favorite show, not because you need the subscription to live. Wants are things you enjoy that you spend money on by choice, such as:

- Subscriptions

sources.title: An essential guide to building an emergency fund | Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
sources.text: There are different strategies to get your savings started. These strategies cover a range of situations, including if you have a limited ability to save or if your pay tends to fluctuate. It may be that you could use all of these strategies, but if you have a limited ability to save, managing your cash flow or putting away a portion of your tax refund are the easiest ways to get started.
